title: The Jungle Book
author: d'après Rudyard Kipling
desc: Mowgli, le petit d'homme élevé par les loups, face au tigre Shere Khan.

p: One warm evening in the Indian jungle, Father Wolf and Mother Wolf heard a noise near their cave. A little human baby was standing there, naked, laughing.
"A man-cub!" said Father Wolf. "Look how small he is."
Then a huge shadow arrived at the cave. It was Shere Khan, the tiger. "Give me the man-cub!" he roared. "He is my dinner!"
Mother Wolf stood in front of the baby. Her eyes were like fire. "He is mine now! Go away, Shere Khan, or I will fight you!"
The tiger was too big to enter the cave. He went away, angry. "One day, he will be mine!"
Mother Wolf looked at the baby. "I will call you Mowgli. It means 'little frog'."
The wolves of the Pack met at the Council Rock. Can a man-cub live with wolves? Two animals spoke for him.
The first was Baloo, the big, sleepy brown bear. "I will teach him the Law of the Jungle," he said.
The second was Bagheera, the black panther. She was elegant and dangerous. "I will give a fat bull to the Pack if you accept him," she said.
So Mowgli grew up with the wolves. Baloo taught him the words of every animal. Bagheera taught him to climb trees and to hunt.
Mowgli was happy. But Bagheera often looked at him with worried eyes. "One day, little brother, you must go back to the humans. Shere Khan is waiting."
Years passed. Mowgli became a strong boy. But Shere Khan talked to the young wolves. "Why do you obey an old leader and a human?" he said.
Bagheera told Mowgli: "Go to the village. Bring back the Red Flower. All animals are afraid of it."
The Red Flower was fire. Mowgli took burning coals from a village house in a pot.
At the Council Rock, Shere Khan and the young wolves attacked. Mowgli lifted a burning branch. The animals screamed and ran away. He hit Shere Khan with the fire, and the tiger ran into the night.
Then Mowgli cried for the first time. "Tears are human things," said Bagheera softly. "You are a man now, little brother."

Mowgli went to live in the human village. A woman called Messua took him into her home. He learned to wear clothes and to speak the language of men. Every day, he took the village buffaloes to the fields.
One day, his wolf brother Grey Brother came to see him. "Shere Khan is coming for you tomorrow, in the ravine."

Mowgli had a plan. With the wolves, he divided the buffaloes into two groups. They ran into the ravine from both sides. Shere Khan was trapped between them. The huge buffaloes ran over the tiger, and Shere Khan was never seen again.
Mowgli put the tiger's skin on the Council Rock. He had kept his promise. But now he belonged to two worlds: the jungle and the village. And like many of us, he had to learn to live between the two.
